name: Souks & Central Market
hero_subtitle: Spices, fresh fish and the daily pulse of the city.

overview.title: The commercial heart of El Jadida
overview.p1: The central market and souks of El Jadida offer fresh fish, fruit, spices and a few crafts. The atmosphere is local and lively, especially in the morning.
overview.p2: It is a good place to buy the day's catch or simply to soak up everyday life away from the citadel's tourist path.
overview.p3: Combine with a port visit and lunch on the quay for a full maritime morning.

1.title: Best time
1.desc: Fresh produce and lively stalls; ideal for fish and spices.

2.title: Busier
2.desc: More people; some stalls start to close.

3.title: Quieter
3.desc: Fewer vendors; good for a short stroll.

food.title: Eating near the market
food.p1: Restaurants are mainly around the port and the corniche, a short walk away.
food.li1: Fish restaurants at the port (5–10 min walk).
food.li3: Simple tables in the citadel streets.
food.p2: Cash remains useful for small local places.
food.li4: Avoid eating inside heritage sites (no facilities).
food.li5: Bring water before or after the visit.

1.title: Opening hours
1.desc: Best in the morning; some stalls close early afternoon.

2.title: Photos
2.desc: Ask before photographing vendors; be discreet.

3.title: Bargaining
3.desc: Normal for crafts; fish and produce are usually fixed price.

q1.question: How much time for the souks?
q1.answer: 30 to 60 minutes is enough for a good stroll through the central market.

q2.question: Is it mainly tourist-oriented?
q2.answer: No — it is a local market for everyday shopping, with a genuine atmosphere.

q3.question: Can I buy fresh fish?
q3.answer: Yes, the fish stalls are one of the main attractions, especially in the morning.

q4.question: Is bargaining expected?
q4.answer: For crafts yes; for fish and produce prices are usually fixed.

q5.question: How to get there?
q5.answer: In the city centre, a short walk from the Portuguese City and the port.
